what: Independent review of the steering run additions at 925550e0 (r_heat_peak, whole-robot mass and payload, dev presets, notebook menu): two reviewers (correctness, design), each followed by a skeptic who re-checked every finding. Given the code and the records, not the author's conclusions.

findings.title: Step 8's mj_setConst overwrites the reset state: every episode with the whole-robot ranges starts from qpos_spring (neck at -0.54 rad, outside its limit; no leg joint noise; soles at 0 mm, not 2 mm)
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py, reset() step 8, the line mujoco.mj_setConst(m, d) followed by mujoco.mj_forward(m, d) (about line 863)
findings.evidence: MuJoCo 3.10.0's mj_setConst rewrites d.qpos. After 10 steps of an episode, a call to mj_setConst changed qpos by up to 0.56, while qvel, ctrl, act, mocap_pos and sensordata stayed the same (scratchpad/review_steer/setconst_state.py). In reset, step 4 has already set the home keyframe, the +-0.02 rad leg noise and the 2 mm sole clearance, and step 8 then calls mj_setConst, which overwrites all of it. Same seed, with and without the ranges (reset_state.py, reset_state2.py): the 12 leg joints come out exactly 0 (the noise is gone), the root sits at z 0.3200 instead of about 0.323, and the lowest sole is at -0.0000 instead of 0.0020. neck_pitch is -0.5395, which is the model's qpos_spring for that joint (neck.py) and lies outside its range of +-0.349 rad. One joint-limit constraint is active at every reset. The ranges set to (1.0, 1.0) and (0.0, 0.0), which change no mass, give the identical clobbered state. Effect on the preset steer1_dev_heat1 (transient.py, snap.py): the neck snaps back at a peak of 8.1 rad/s against 1.0 rad/s without the ranges. Every reset is now the same settled pose: the chassis's peak angular velocity in the first 0.5 s is 0.008 rad/s against 0.107 rad/s. So reset_joint_noise and the clearance drop are silently off in both dev presets and in any judged run that uses them. Every randomised evaluation (H2) also starts this way. The existing test checks only total mass, inertia and subtree mass, so it passes. The tests and both digests pass because the default config never reaches step 8.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the state across the constant recomputation. In step 8: q, v = d.qpos.copy(), d.qvel.copy(); mujoco.mj_setConst(m, d); d.qpos[:] = q; d.qvel[:] = v; mujoco.mj_forward(m, d). Tested in a scratch subclass (fix_check.py): qpos and masses then match the no-range config exactly for seeds 0-2, and the sole clearance is back at 0.002. The reset obs still differ, as expected, because the two extra uniforms shift the later observation-noise stream. Add a test: for the same seed, the config with mass_scale_whole_range=(1,1) and payload_kg_range=(0,0) gives a d.qpos after reset array_equal to the config without them, with the neck inside its range and _lowest_sole_z() equal to reset_sole_clearance.

findings.title: The evaluation tools inherit the whole-robot ranges. flat_floor() does not clear them, so every randomised measure (gait report target case, steer_eval, PeriodicEval, evaluate.py, the sweep's reproduction point) now runs on a robot about 4 % heavier on average, up to x1.15
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py FLAT_FLOOR / flat_floor(); consumers: train.py PeriodicEval (domain_randomization=True) and the checks' steering courses, steer_eval.make_env, analytics/gait_report.py CASES target_0.25 and cmd_0.15, evaluate.py (randomisation on by default), robustness/sweep.py build_env(randomise=True) (the reproduction point)
findings.evidence: Built each tool's env from the run record that train.py writes for steer1_dev_heat1 (tools_inherit.py). PeriodicEval, steer_eval.make_env, gait_report target_0.25, evaluate.py's default and the sweep's reproduction point all have DR on, apply the whole factor and the payload, and start with neck -0.54 (H1). gait_report nominal_0.25, the sweep's points (randomise=False), foot_loads.py and demo_course.py run with DR off and stay nominal. The D22 judge takes F2's figure (H_all) from gait_report's target_0.25 case (judge_d22.py lines 15 and 144). On the five gait_pipe1.SEEDS of that case, the mass/nominal ratios are [1.145, 1.000, 0.961, 1.030, 0.933] with the new ranges and [1.034, 0.949, 0.995, 1.018, 0.963] without. Over 300 seeds: mean 1.044 (5-95 %: 0.939-1.146) with them, against 1.000 (0.958-1.044) without (target_mass.py). The plan treats 'the whole robot 10 % heavier' as a separate stress point and the target case as nominal whole mass. As built, one of the five target-case seeds is already heavier than that stress point. The target-case heat figure would then be biased against the new run and could not be compared with F20's 0.83-0.95 for 128 mm. The dev runs' eval_during_training heat lines (3 episodes) carry this extra mass spread too.
findings.suggested_fix: Make it an explicit choice before the dev runs. Recommended: add 'mass_scale_whole_range': None and 'payload_kg_range': None to FLAT_FLOOR (and to the copy in robustness/sweep.py FLAT_FLOOR, which config_diffs uses). The evaluations then randomise per body only, as in D22; older runs' configs are unchanged, since they hold None. The stress points (x1.1 whole mass, payload) stay in the sweep. Add a test that flat_floor() of a steer1 preset config builds an env whose total mass after reset matches the same config without the ranges. If the owner instead wants evaluations inside the widened training distribution, say so in the pre-registration and keep a nominal-whole-mass target case for the heat rule.

findings.title: In 2-3 M step dev runs the hottest-drive cost almost never reaches full weight (default late ramp 1 M -> 3 M), so the dev runs cannot set w_heat_peak for 10 M judged runs
findings.location: train.py --late-ramp-from / --late-ramp-to defaults (1,000,000 / 3,000,000); trike60_training.ipynb (TOTAL_STEPS default 2,000,000; no late-ramp parameter); r_heat_peak listed in LATE_TERMS
findings.evidence: r_heat_peak = -w_heat_peak x late_scale x excess (trike_env.py reward_terms), and train.py ramps late_scale linearly from 1 M to 3 M steps. Computed: a 3 M step run (D30's 'about 3 M') ends at late_scale 1.00, with a mean of 0.33 and 0.0 % of its steps at full weight. A run at the notebook's default TOTAL_STEPS of 2 M ends at 0.50, with a mean of 0.13. The notebook's train command passes no --late-ramp-*, and a preset cannot set them because they are train.py arguments, not env config. Pushes and the slippery-floor end follow --terrain-ramp 1 M -> 4 M, so they reach only 0.67 of full scale by 3 M. In the 4096-step check run with the ramp forced to 0 -> 1, r_heat_peak at weight 3 was -0.37 to -0.83 per step against r_heat's -0.21 (train_health.jsonl). So the weight matters, but the default schedule hides it in a 3 M step run.
findings.suggested_fix: For the dev runs, either expose LATE_RAMP_FROM and LATE_RAMP_TO (and the terrain ramp) in the notebook and use an earlier, shorter ramp (for example 0.5 M -> 1.5 M), or make the dev runs long enough to spend at least 1-2 M steps at full weight. State in the run steps that TOTAL_STEPS must be 3 M or more and which ramp the judged 10 M runs will use, so that the dev runs test the same schedule.

findings.title: The effective weight of the low-passed cost is much lower than w_heat_peak suggests (cold-start EMA each reset, 4 s tau against gamma 0.99, state hidden from the critic). Undocumented, and it matters for choosing between weights 1 and 3
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py step() heat_peak block; _reset_episode_state (self._heat_ema = np.zeros(12)); TrikeEnvConfig w_heat_peak/heat_peak_tau_s comments
findings.evidence: The formula is right: the per-drive sum over physics steps / frame_skip, then EMA alpha = 1 - exp(-0.02/4) = 0.00499 per control step, then max, then sqrt, then max(0, . - margin). The independent recomputation test agrees to 1e-12. But the EMA restarts at 0 on every reset. For a drive held exactly at its rating (RMS 1.0), the cost first appears at t = 4.08 s, and the mean cost over a 20 s episode is 61 % of the steady 0.20. At RMS 0.90 the cost first appears at 6.24 s and the mean is 50 %; at 0.85, 8.66 s and 38 %. An episode that ends early pays almost nothing. With gamma 0.99, a step's (torque/rating)^2 reaches the discounted return through the EMA with a weight of sum g^k alpha (1-alpha)^k = 0.334, against 1.0 for an unfiltered per-step cost. Neither the EMA nor the elapsed time is in the observation (phase clock off), so the critic cannot predict the term. In effect, weights 1 and 3 behave roughly like 0.2-0.33 and 0.6-1.0 of a per-step cost, which the config comments do not say.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the effective scaling next to w_heat_peak and in the dev-run notes. Consider starting each episode's EMA at a warm value (for example the first step's mean, or a nominal standing value) rather than 0, and/or a shorter heat_peak_tau_s (1-2 s), or give the critic the 12 EMAs (or the hottest one) as a privileged observation. Decide before the dev runs, since changing it afterwards invalidates the weight they choose.

findings.title: The steer1 presets do not pin the model and the notebook's MODEL default is trike60_C_closed, so selecting a steer1 preset alone trains on the wrong model (D25: fore128)
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike60_training.ipynb cell 1 (MODEL default, ENV_PRESET check); configs/steer1_dev_heat1.json, steer1_dev_heat3.json
findings.evidence: In the notebook, MODEL = "trike60_C_closed" is the default. train.env_config builds model_path from --model, and the presets carry no model_path. No guard ties ENV_PRESET steer1_* to MODEL trike60_C_closed_capsule_fore128, and no run-steps file for the steering runs exists yet (grep steer1 finds only the notebook). A run on the wrong model would show up only in run_record.json, after the Colab time is spent.
findings.suggested_fix: In cell 1, refuse ENV_PRESET steer1_* unless MODEL == "trike60_C_closed_capsule_fore128" ('Nothing was run.'), or write the model into the run-steps document for these runs.

findings.title: The sweep's training-range shading and report text still say delay 0-10 ms and per-body mass only, so for the steering runs the plan's stress points (20 ms, x1.1 whole mass, payload) would be shown as outside training
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/robustness/sweep.py TRAINING / training_ranges() (about lines 64-75) and the hard-coded 'Training ranges: ...' line (about line 680)
findings.evidence: training_ranges(ec) on the steer1 run record returns {'delay_ms': (0, 10), 'friction': (0.3, 1.0), 'mass_scale': (0.9, 1.1), ...}. It reads friction from the record, but not delay_steps_range [0, 20], mass_scale_whole_range or payload_kg_range. The report text is a fixed string ('delay 0-10 ms ... mass and inertia x0.9-1.1 per body ... flat floor, no pushes'). The fixed string was already stale for run 3; the new ranges add to that.
findings.suggested_fix: Read delay_steps_range, mass_scale_whole_range and payload_kg_range (and push_prob) from the record in training_ranges(), and generate the report's 'Training ranges' sentence from it.

findings.title: Minor: the LATE_TERMS line is 127 characters (repo line length 120), and heat_peak_rms is not in the training-health log
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py line 59; telemetry/health.py collects only keys with the prefixes r_ and reward_
findings.evidence: awk finds trike_env.py:59 at 127 characters; pyproject.toml has line-length = 120. info['heat_peak_rms'] is computed every step but has no r_ prefix, so train_health.jsonl records only r_heat_peak (a cost that is 0 below the margin and before the late ramp). The quantity the dev runs are meant to tune, the hottest drive's running RMS, is therefore not visible during training.

checked_ok: Tests: test_steer_heat.py, 13 passed; test_trike_env.py, all 94 passed (exit 0). Both regression digests (test_default_env_regression_digest and test_run3_env_regression_digest) PASS and are not skipped (mujoco 3.10.0); git status --short is empty before and after.

Heat term arithmetic: per-drive tau^2/rating^2 summed over the 20 physics steps and divided by frame_skip; EMA alpha = 1 - exp(-control dt / tau), updated once per control step (correct for dt = 0.02 s); sqrt of the max = max of the sqrt; max(0, . - margin); sign negative; multiplied by late_scale; exactly -0.0 == 0 when w_heat_peak = 0 (no accumulation, heat_peak_rms stays 0). heat_vec uses the same idx/inv_c2 ordering as the existing r_heat, so its sum / (12 frame_skip) equals heat_index.

r_heat_peak is in REWARD_TERMS and LATE_TERMS; the test assertion on LATE_TERMS is updated; train.py has no hard-coded term list; telemetry/health.py picks it up through the r_ prefix (seen in a real train_health.jsonl: -0.37 to -0.83 at weight 3 with late_scale 1); analytics/training_dashboard and the checks have no fixed term list; REWARD_BONUSES' '<= 0' convention holds.

Whole-robot factors: applied after _apply_factors (per-body) and undone by _restore_nominal on the next reset (no accumulation, as tested); world body excluded via [1:]; inertia scaled with mass; payload on the chassis with chassis inertia x the same mass ratio, the same as robustness/sweep.apply_point; mj_setConst then mj_forward; factors recorded; DR off draws but does not apply; the draws come after the steering draw, so the request schedule is unchanged (tested); terrain arrays (mocap pose, geom_size, rbound, aabb, bvh) are not disturbed by the extra mj_setConst (terrain_check.py).

Cached values: nominal_height is not materially stale (standing height 0.3190 at 15.03 kg against 0.3192 nominal; r_height about 0); the model has no gravcomp; the push force uses the current total mass (model.body_mass.sum() at onset), so dv is preserved under payload; _sat_limit depends only on forcerange; the foot-load observation is normalised by the fixed nominal weight (as a real robot's would be).

Validation: negative w_heat_peak, margin 0, tau 0, reversed range, whole low 0 and negative payload are refused (tested). Edge cases reasoned or run: a margin above every value gives 0; a tiny tau gives alpha -> 1 (the step mean); payload 0 skips the chassis change; whole (1,1) leaves masses unchanged (but still triggers H1).
Delay 0-20 ms: the FIFO length is delay+1 (21), both ends are drawn over 200 seeds, and the state stays finite.

Vectorised path: a 4096-step train.py run with --vec subproc, 2 envs, steer1_dev_heat3 completed with checkpoints and PeriodicEval; the run record stores w_heat_peak 3.0, margin 0.8, tau 4.0, the whole range [0.9, 1.1], payload [0.0, 1.0] and delay [0, 20]; the config survives to_dict/from_dict into the workers.

DR-off tools (gait_report nominal_0.25, the sweep's points, the training checks' sweep points, foot_loads.py, demo_course.py) run the nominal model, unaffected by the new ranges except for two extra unapplied uniforms that shift later observation-noise draws (harmless).

verdicts.reasoning: I re-ran it myself and it holds. In reset(), step 4 sets the keyframe, the leg noise and the 2 mm sole clearance. Step 8 then calls mujoco.mj_setConst(m, d), which in MuJoCo 3.10.0 leaves d.qpos equal to m.qpos_spring. The leg noise and the clearance are lost, and the neck starts outside its joint limit. This happens whenever either range is set, even (1,1)/(0,0), whether or not any mass changes. Both dev presets reach it. The default config never reaches step 8, so the digests and the new tests (13 passed) do not catch it. Restoring qpos and qvel around mj_setConst fixes it.

'with' and 'unit' (1,1)/(0,0) give: leg deviation from the keyframe 0.0000, root z 0.3200, lowest sole -0.0000, neck_pitch -0.5395 against range +-0.349, nefc 17 (efc types include 3 = joint limit). 'without' gives: leg deviation 0.018-0.020, root z 0.3226-0.3239, sole 0.0020, neck 0.0, nefc 0. Directly checked: np.allclose(d.qpos, m.qpos_spring) is True; max|qpos - key_qpos| = 0.539. h1b.py, first 0.5 s, 5 seeds: neck peak speed 7.9-8.3 rad/s against 0.79-1.09 without; chassis peak angular velocity 0.007-0.009 against 0.056-0.149 rad/s. h1c.py, with q and v kept across mj_setConst: the unit-range qpos is array_equal to the no-range qpos for seeds 0-2, the sole is at 0.0020 and nefc is 0. pytest test_steer_heat.py: all pass; git status clean.

verdicts.reasoning: This holds. FLAT_FLOOR in trike_env.py and in robustness/sweep.py, and gait_pipe1.flat_floor, clear only terrain_boxes, push_prob and friction_low_hard. Every evaluation built from a steer1 run record therefore keeps mass_scale_whole_range and payload_kg_range, and applies them wherever DR is on: PeriodicEval forces domain_randomization=True, as do gait_report's target_0.25 and cmd_0.15 cases, evaluate.py's default and the sweep's randomise=True. verdicts.reasoning: The arithmetic holds: the EMA restarts at zero, the 4 s time constant delays the cost, the discounted weight is about 0.33, and neither the EMA nor the elapsed time is observed. But this is a documented design choice: the low-pass and its tau are in the config comment, and the reset to zeros is visible. It is not a defect that makes the runs wrong. The env already uses unobserved low-passed states in its costs (lateral_drift_tau_s 1 s, track_yaw_tau_s 0.5 s). The dev runs choose the weight from measured outcomes, so the effective scaling is built into whatever weight they pick. The claim that it 'matters for choosing between 1 and 3' is overstated. findings.title: Step 8's mj_setConst(m, d) overwrites the placed reset state: no leg reset noise, soles start in contact instead of 2 mm up, in every episode of both presets
findings.evidence: MuJoCo 3.10.0. mj_setConst(m, d) rewrites d.qpos indices 7-26, so the leg joints go back to 0, and resets the root z to 0.3200. Step 8 runs after the state was placed in step 4. Test: with unit factors (mass_scale_whole_range (1,1), payload_kg_range (0,0)), the masses are identical, but reset seeds 0-2 give a different qpos from the config without the factors. The leg joints read all 0.000 instead of the +-0.02 rad reset noise. Chassis z is 0.3200 instead of 0.3239. The lowest sole is at -1e-10 m instead of the 2 mm clearance. Over 200 identical steps (obs noise and drift off) qpos then diverges by up to 0.46. When qpos is saved before mj_setConst and restored after, the same comparison is bit-identical (max qpos diff 0.0 over 200 steps). Also, mj_setConst on a scratch MjData gives identical model constants (subtreemass, invweight0, acc0, length0). Both presets have randomisation on, so this hits every training reset. It also hits every randomised measurement: the gait report target case (verified: seeds 100000-100004 have no leg noise and sole z 0.0000), steer_eval, evaluate.py and train.py's periodic evals. Terrain mocap positions survive, so a later terrain run would only lose qpos. test_steer_heat.py checks masses and subtree mass, never the state.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 8, compute the constants without touching the live state. Either call mujoco.mj_setConst(m, self._const_data), where self._const_data = mujoco.MjData(m) is made once in __init__, or save d.qpos (and d.qvel) before mj_setConst(m, d) and restore them before mj_forward. Add a test: with unit factors and observation noise and drift off, reset qpos and a 200-step trajectory equal the config without the factors bit for bit, and _lowest_sole_z() is about reset_sole_clearance.

findings.title: The new mass and payload draws leak into the judged measurements: the flat-floor reductions keep them, so the F1/F2 target case and the 0.85 heat rule are measured on a robot of random total mass
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/trike_env.py:405 (FLAT_FLOOR); rl/analysis/gait_pipe1.py:82-88 (flat_floor, own copy); rl/robustness/sweep.py:199 (FLAT_FLOOR copy); callers analytics/gait_report.py:630, steer_eval.py:51, train.py:503

findings.title: A 3 M-step dev run never trains with the heat cost at full weight, so it cannot set the weight the 10 M judged runs will use
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/train.py:126-134 (late ramp 1 M to 3 M, terrain ramp 1 M to 4 M), :734 (LR linear over total steps); rl/PLAN_STEERING_RUN.md 'The runs'
findings.evidence: r_heat_peak is in LATE_TERMS. In a 3 M run, late_scale is 0 until 1 M, 0.5 at 2 M and 1.0 only at the last rollout: a mean of 0.75 over the last 1 M and 0 steps at full weight, against about 7 M steps in a 10 M judged run. The learning rate (3e-4 to 3e-5 linear over TOTAL_STEPS) is 2.1e-4, 1.2e-4 and 3e-5 at 1, 2 and 3 M in a 3 M run, against 2.7e-4, 2.5e-4 and 2.2e-4 in a 10 M run. So the dev policy is annealing just as the cost arrives. The terrain scale reaches only 0.67 at 3 M: pushes up to 0.67 m/s instead of 1.0, and a friction low end of 0.40 instead of 0.30. A weight-driven change in gait, or a late collapse towards standing (M2), would appear in the judged runs but not in the dev runs. Seed noise: fore128's hottest drive spans 0.828-0.945 over 4 seeds at identical settings (gait reports). One seed per weight cannot resolve differences under about 0.1.
findings.suggested_fix: Start each dev run with TOTAL_STEPS = 10,000,000, so the LR, late and terrain schedules are identical to the judged runs, and stop it with the notebook's stop button at about 5 M. Read the 5 M checkpoint: about 2.5 h each at the plan's 1.5 h per 3 M, with 2 M steps at full heat weight and 1 M at full pushes and friction. The second-best option is TOTAL_STEPS 5 M (the LR then differs). Give both dev runs the same SEED, read the per-episode worst drive and the sweep's x1.1 and 20 ms points, and treat a weight effect under about 0.1 RMS as unresolved. Update the plan's '3 M, 1.5 h' wording.

findings.title: Weight 3 likely makes standing beat a noisy 128 mm gait at full scale, the failure the README's weight rule was set to avoid; weight 1 halves that margin
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/configs/steer1_dev_heat1.json, steer1_dev_heat3.json (w_heat_peak); rl/README.md reward-table section (0.366 margin rule)
findings.evidence: Measured with the README's method: seeds 100000-100002, 0.25 m/s, delay 10 ms, randomisation on, late and penalty scale 1, 20 s. The initial-policy noise (std 0.2 around 0) has its hottest drive at EMA RMS 1.07-1.15 and costs r_heat_peak -0.22 per step at w=1 (-0.66 at w=3). Standing's hottest drive is 0.47-0.58 (0.58 at x1.1 plus 1 kg), so standing pays 0. That makes the new term alone at w=3 about 1.5x all existing late costs on noise (README: heat -0.22, saturation -0.08, air-time -0.13). The next figures are estimated, not measured (no checkpoint was run). A walking gait at F20's 0.95 with noise is about 1.08 (the README's noise ratio 0.99/0.76 in mean square), which costs 0.28 per step steady and 0.19 as a 20 s episode mean per unit w. The README's noisy walking minus standing margin of +0.366 then becomes about +0.18 at w=1 and -0.20 at w=3; the README rejected heat 0.5 / saturation 5 for -0.03. At F20's x1.1-mass worst of 1.22 the cost is 0.42 (w=1) or 1.26 (w=3) per step. The policy can sense extra mass through foot_load_over_weight (normalised by nominal weight), so it can learn to slow or stand in heavy episodes. Two things soften this. Under gamma 0.99 the 4 s lag means the return sees only f = alpha/(1-gamma(1-alpha)) = 0.33 of the price, so the effective weights are about 0.33 and 1.0. And the cost bites mostly on fast requests: the hottest drive is 0.70-0.83 at 0.15 m/s against 0.83-0.95 at 0.25 m/s. Tracking still dominates small speed shortfalls: 0.03 m/s under costs 0.36 per step against at most 0.21 saved at w=3.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the dev runs, add r_heat_peak to the README's 'reward per step at three stages' measurement for a fore128 policy plus noise against standing (a few minutes), and pick weights that keep the noisy-walking margin at 0.3 or more at full scale, or record why not. Consider bracketing 0.5-1 and 1.5-2 rather than 1 and 3, or keep 1 and 3 only with the 10 M-schedule dev runs from M1 so a collapse would show. In the pre-registration, require walking (F1-like speed, no falls) at the heat stress points, not heat alone. State the effective weight (w x f) next to the nominal one.

findings.title: The heat average restarts from 0 at every reset, so the cost is off for the first 5-9 s of each 20 s episode exactly where 128 mm sits (0.83-0.95)
findings.evidence: With a constant per-step heat r^2, tau 4 s and margin 0.8, the first costed step comes at 8.7, 6.3, 4.9 and 4.1 s for a steady hottest RMS of 0.85, 0.90, 0.95 and 1.00. The 20 s episode cost is then 0.38, 0.50, 0.57 and 0.61 of the steady cost, and 0.42-0.68 over F2's own 2-20 s window. F2 counts the whole 18 s window at full value. So the cost under-prices most strongly the band it is meant to move (F20: 0.83-0.95). The average is not observed, so the critic sees identical observations at 1 s (cost 0) and 15 s (cost on): added value noise.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a bias-corrected average: keep a step count n since reset and price sqrt(E_n / (1 - (1-alpha)^n)). It equals the running mean since reset early on, which is F2's own estimator, and the EMA later. If the settling transient matters, start the average at 2 s, as F2's window does. Add a test that a constant heat input gives a constant heat_peak_rms from the first step.

findings.title: The 4 s filter charges short push-recovery bursts that neither F2's 18 s window nor the 4-15 min windings register
findings.evidence: Against a stride the 4 s time constant is fine: at 0.67-1 Hz the average passes 1/17-1/25 of the stride's oscillation. Against physics, the thermal constants are 240-900 s (telemetry/thermal.py TIME_CONSTANTS_S), 60-225x longer. Example: a drive held at 0.70 that bursts to 2x rating for 0.5 s (a push recovery; the X4 limit is about 2.8x) keeps its 18 s RMS at 0.766, under the margin. That burst costs 14.3 per unit w (7.1 discounted) at tau 4 s, 24.8 at tau 2 s and 0 at tau 18 s. At w=3 that is about 43, about 9 termination penalties. Pushes come in 50 % of the preset's episodes, and F20 found 128 mm already falls more under hard pushes. Longer tau is not free: under gamma 0.99 the share of the price seen is 0.67, 0.50, 0.33, 0.20 and 0.10 at tau 1, 2, 4, 8 and 18 s.
findings.suggested_fix: If push robustness drops in the dev runs, gate the price instead: charge each drive's per-step excess heat, w x (x_i,t - m^2)/(2m), only while that drive's slow average (tau 10-18 s, bias-corrected) is above the margin. That gives F2-like selection with immediate credit (f about 1), and bursts on a cool drive stay free. Either way, document tau's trade-off in the config comment.

findings.title: Only the single hottest drive is priced, though 128 mm usually has two or three drives above 0.8
findings.evidence: Target-case hottest and next drives in the fore128 gait reports: s0 0.828/0.815; s1 0.888/0.811; s2 0.931/0.857/0.822; s3 0.945/0.901. With max(), cooling the hottest drive pays only down to the runner-up's level, and the gradient falls on one drive at a time, which changes from episode to episode. findings.suggested_fix: Keep the max form per D29, or ask the owner whether a sum of hinges, sum_i max(0, r_i - 0.8), is acceptable. It prices every drive that could fail F2 ('every joint under 1.0'). At the 128 mm baselines it costs 1.0-1.7x the max form (s3: 0.246 against 0.145), so the weights would need rescaling.
